name: Plank
summary: Holding your body in a straight line on forearms and toes. It trains the trunk to resist sagging, a skill you need in almost every other lift.
steps: Kneel on a mat and place your forearms on the floor, elbows directly under your shoulders and forearms parallel.
Step your feet back one at a time until your body forms a straight line from head to heels, feet hip-width apart.
Tuck your tailbone slightly, squeeze your glutes and tighten your abs as if bracing for a nudge.
Push your forearms into the floor so your upper back does not sag between your shoulder blades. Look at the floor just ahead of your hands.
Breathe steadily and hold for the planned time, stopping when your hips start to sag. Lower your knees to finish.
mistakes: Hips sagging and the lower back arching
Hips piked up high to make it easier
Holding your breath
Chasing long times with sloppy form instead of short, tight holds
easier: Hold the plank from your knees, or with your forearms on a bench.
harder: Lift one foot a few centimeters for a few seconds at a time, or reach one arm forward without shifting your hips.

name: Side Plank
summary: A plank on one forearm with your body turned sideways. It trains the obliques and hip muscles to stop your trunk bending sideways, a gap in many routines.
steps: Lie on your side on a mat with your elbow directly under your shoulder and your forearm pointing straight ahead. Stack your legs and feet.
Tighten your abs and glutes, then lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from head to feet.
Keep your hips pushed forward and stacked one above the other, not rolling toward the floor or the ceiling.
Rest your top hand on your hip or reach it toward the ceiling, and keep your neck in line with your spine.
Hold while breathing steadily, lower with control, then repeat on the other side.
cues: Push the floor away with your forearm
Long line from head to heels
mistakes: Letting the hips drop toward the floor
Sitting the hips back, so the body bends at the waist
Sinking into the supporting shoulder
Rolling the chest toward the floor
easier: Bend your knees and support yourself on your forearm and bottom knee.
harder: Lift the top leg, or lower and raise your hips slowly for reps.

name: Dead Bug
summary: Lying on your back and lowering the opposite arm and leg while your lower back stays put. It teaches your abs to hold your spine steady while your limbs move.
steps: Lie on your back with your arms pointing straight up at the ceiling and your hips and knees bent to 90 degrees, shins parallel to the floor.
Breathe out, draw your ribs down and gently press your lower back toward the floor.
Slowly lower your right arm overhead and straighten your left leg toward the floor at the same time, keeping your lower back in place.
Stop just before your hand and heel touch the floor, or as soon as your back starts to arch.
Return to the start and repeat with the left arm and right leg. Keep alternating slowly.
cues: Lower back stays heavy on the floor
Move slowly, as if through water
mistakes: Letting the lower back arch off the floor as the leg lowers
Rushing through the reps
Holding your breath
Moving the arm and leg on the same side
easier: Move only the legs, or tap the heel to the floor with the knee still bent.
harder: Hold a light weight in your hands, or pause for three seconds in the extended position.

name: Bird Dog
summary: From hands and knees, you reach one arm and the opposite leg while keeping your trunk still. A gentle, widely used drill for back and hip control.
steps: Kneel on all fours with hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips. Keep your back flat and look at the floor.
Tighten your midsection gently, as if bracing for a light poke.
Slide one leg straight back and lift it to hip height while reaching the opposite arm forward to shoulder height.
Hold for two to five seconds with hips and shoulders level, as if balancing a glass of water on your lower back.
Return your hand and knee to the floor under control, then repeat on the other side.
cues: Hips stay square to the floor
Do not spill the glass on your back
mistakes: Lifting the leg too high and arching the lower back
Rotating the hips open as the leg lifts
Shifting the weight far to one side
Rushing instead of pausing in the reach
easier: Move only an arm or only a leg at a time, sliding the foot back along the floor without lifting it.
harder: Hold each reach for 10 seconds, or bring elbow and knee together under your body between reps.

name: Hollow Hold
summary: A gymnastics staple: lying on your back and holding a shallow banana shape with shoulders and legs off the floor. It builds serious strength in the front of the trunk.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees pulled toward your chest and your arms by your sides. Press your lower back firmly into the floor.
Lift your head and shoulder blades slightly off the floor, tucking your chin gently.
Straighten your legs up and out, lowering them only as far as you can keep your lower back pressed down.
Reach your arms overhead beside your ears if you can hold the position, or keep them pointing toward your feet.
Hold while taking short, steady breaths. Stop when your lower back starts to lift, then hug your knees to rest.
cues: Lower back glued to the floor
mistakes: Letting the lower back arch off the floor
Dropping the legs lower than the abs can control
Pulling the chin hard to the chest and straining the neck
Holding your breath
easier: Keep your knees bent over your hips (a tuck hold), or straighten only one leg.
harder: Reach your arms overhead with legs low, or rock gently forward and back while holding the shape.

name: Pallof Press
summary: Pressing a band or cable straight out from your chest while it tries to twist you sideways. It trains your trunk to resist rotation without bending or twisting the spine.
steps: Anchor a band to a sturdy post at chest height, or set a cable pulley to the same height. Stand side-on to the anchor.
Hold the band with both hands against your breastbone and step away until it is taut. Set your feet shoulder-width apart with knees soft.
Brace your midsection and squeeze your glutes, with shoulders and hips square to the front.
Press your hands straight out in front of your chest until your arms are straight, resisting the pull toward the anchor.
Hold for two to three seconds, then bring your hands back to your chest slowly.
Complete your reps, then turn around and repeat facing the other way.
cues: Belt buckle and chest face forward
Do not let the band turn you
mistakes: Letting the hands drift toward the anchor
Rotating or leaning the torso to counter the pull
Shrugging the shoulders up
Standing so close that there is no real tension
easier: Use a lighter band, stand closer to the anchor, or take a wider stance.
harder: Step further away, narrow your stance, or hold each press for five to ten seconds.

name: Hanging Knee Raise
summary: Hanging from a bar and lifting your knees toward your chest. It works the abs and hip flexors hard, and builds grip and shoulder strength as a bonus.
steps: Grip a pull-up bar with palms facing away, hands shoulder-width apart, and hang with arms straight.
Pull your shoulders down, away from your ears, and tighten your abs so your body is still.
Lift your knees toward your chest, curling your pelvis up slightly at the top so your abs finish the movement.
Pause briefly with your knees at or above hip height.
Lower your legs slowly until they are straight, and stop any swing before the next rep.
cues: Curl the hips up, not just the knees
Lower slowly to kill the swing
mistakes: Swinging the legs and using momentum
Hanging limp from the shoulders
Dropping the legs quickly
Arching the lower back at the bottom
easier: Do lying knee tucks on the floor, or use a captain's chair that supports your forearms.
harder: Raise straight legs to hip height, or slow the lowering to four seconds.

name: Mountain Climber
summary: Driving your knees toward your chest from a push-up position. Part core drill, part cardio, it challenges your trunk to stay steady while your legs move fast.
steps: Start in a high plank with hands under your shoulders, arms straight and body in a line from head to heels.
Tighten your abs and glutes and press the floor away so your upper back does not sag between your shoulder blades.
Bring one knee toward your chest without letting your hips rise or your foot drag.
Return that foot to the start as you bring the other knee forward, switching legs smoothly.
Continue alternating at a pace you can hold with level hips, then lower your knees to finish.
mistakes: Hips bouncing up and down or piking high
Shoulders drifting back behind the wrists
Lower back sagging as fatigue builds
Going so fast that the movement shrinks to a shuffle
easier: Slow to a deliberate march, or put your hands on a bench or step.
harder: Speed up while keeping your hips still, or bring each knee across toward the opposite elbow.

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
summary: Kneeling and rolling a wheel out in front of you until your body is nearly straight, then pulling it back. One of the hardest tests of how well your abs resist arching.
steps: Kneel on a mat or pad and hold an ab wheel (or a barbell loaded with small round plates) on the floor under your shoulders, arms straight.
Tuck your tailbone slightly, squeeze your glutes and brace your abs so your lower back is flat or gently rounded.
Roll the wheel forward slowly, letting your hips travel forward with it so your body lengthens from knees to hands.
Go only as far as you can without your lower back sagging. At first, that may be about half the full distance.
Pull the wheel back toward your knees with straight arms, using your abs and lats, without pushing your hips back first.
cues: Tuck the tailbone, squeeze the glutes
mistakes: Letting the lower back arch as the wheel rolls out
Rolling further than you can control
Starting the return by pushing the hips back
Bending the elbows and shrugging the shoulders
easier: Roll toward a wall that stops the wheel at a safe distance, or build up with planks and dead bugs first.
harder: Roll out a little further over time, or pause for two seconds at full reach.

name: Russian Twist
summary: Sitting with your torso leaned back and rotating from side to side. Done slowly with a long spine, it trains the obliques to produce and control rotation.
steps: Sit on a mat with knees bent and heels on the floor. Clasp your hands in front of your chest.
Lean back until you feel your abs switch on, at most about 45 degrees, keeping your chest lifted and your spine long, not slumped.
Rotate your ribcage and shoulders to one side, bringing your hands toward the floor beside your hip. Let your eyes follow your hands.
Pause, then rotate through the center to the other side at the same slow pace.
Keep your knees still and pointing up throughout, and continue alternating for the planned reps.
cues: Turn the ribcage, not just the arms
mistakes: Slumping with a rounded lower back
Swinging the arms from side to side while the torso barely turns
Racing through reps with momentum
Adding weight before the bodyweight version is under control
easier: Sit more upright and reduce the range of the twist.
harder: Hold a medicine ball or light dumbbell, or lift your feet a few centimeters off the floor.
